newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close shade higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close shade higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks pushed shyly higher in slow trading Monday, failing to draw momentum from Wall Street's surge to record highs, dealers said.

"The market is drifting sideways, waiting for the last few company results to trickle in and for U.S. inflation data which should give firm clues as to next week's likely Federal Reserve rate action," said Rodrigo Diz at traders Velox.
The blue-chip MerVal index, which slipped 1.2 percent last week, closed up 0.4 percent at 726.96.
Traders said institutional players kept a low profile, as reflected in the session's thin trading volume of 16.3 million pesos compared with floor turnover of 19.8 million Friday.
Over-the-counter volume also shrank to 49.7 million pesos from 111.5 million Friday.

"We're taking this upward swing on Wall Street with a pinch of salt," an analyst at a large local brokerage said. "Then if the Dow suddenly pulls back tomorrow or the next day, we might be able to hold steady -- we're opting out of this rollercoaster ride at least until we know for sure what the Fed decides."
Diz predicted if the markets cleared the Fed hurdle "the MerVal will head towards 740, steadily but without euphoria."
The broad market index closed up 0.2 percent, with winners edging out losers 23 to 22 and 17 issues closing flat.

The top main-tier gainer was textile firm Alpargatas, which shot up 5.9 percent on restructuring plans after an early profit-taking slump on poor quarterly results, traders said. Steelmaker Siderar and holding Comercial del Plata followed with gains of 3.8 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.
Heaviest MerVal losers were carmaker Sevel, which tumbled 6.9 percent after reporting a first quarter loss of $11.2 million, and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which fell 5.0 percent.
